descripcion_geo: African region south of Egypt, corresponding to present-day Sudan and northern Ethiopia. Cradle of great Nubian pharaohs.
importancia_estrategica: African regional power with Nubian pharaohs who ruled Egypt (25th Dynasty).

historias.titulo: Tirhacah king of Cush comes to the aid of Hezekiah
historias.descripcion: The Ethiopian Pharaoh Tirhaca marches against Sennacherib when Assyria besieges Jerusalem; His arrival precipitates the Assyrian retreat.
Philip the Evangelist finds the Ethiopian queen's treasurer reading Isaiah in his chariot; He baptizes him on the way.

historias.titulo: The rivers of Cush in the prophecies
historias.descripcion: Zephaniah prophesies that worshipers from the rivers of Cush will bring offerings to the Lord from beyond Ethiopia.

personajes.descripcion: Nubian king who ruled Egypt and came to the aid of Hezekiah against the Assyrians.
High Ethiopian official who was baptized by Philip; He brought the gospel to Africa.
Moses's Midianite wife is called 'Cushite' in Numbers, causing family conflict.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Land of mystery and wealth south of the known world; In the NT, the Ethiopian eunuch represents the universality of the gospel.

mitos.nombre: Ethiopia will extend its hands to God

judaismo.descripcion: 'Ethiopia will stretch out her hands to God' (Ps 68:31): promise that African nations will worship the Lord.
judaismo.significado_teologico: 'Ethiopia will stretch out her hands to God' (Ps 68:31): promise that African nations will worship the Lord.

cristianismo.fuente_primaria: Nuevo Testamento / Padres de la Iglesia
cristianismo.descripcion: The baptism of the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8) fulfills the prophecy: the gospel reaches Ethiopia.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The baptism of the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8) fulfills the prophecy: the gospel reaches Ethiopia.
